questions.topic: Logical reasoning & mental ability
questions.question: Find the next term: 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ?
questions.explanation: Each term is (previous × 2) + 1: 63 × 2 + 1 = 127.

questions.topic: Logical reasoning & mental ability
questions.question: Find the next term: 9, 25, 49, 121, ?
questions.explanation: Squares of consecutive primes: 3², 5², 7², 11², so next is 13² = 169. (12² = 144 is the trap.)

questions.topic: Logical reasoning & mental ability
questions.question: Find the next letter: A, C, F, J, O, ?
questions.explanation: Positions 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 increase by 2, 3, 4, 5; the next step is +6, giving 21 = U.

questions.topic: Logical reasoning & mental ability
questions.question: Find the odd one out: 121, 169, 196, 250, 225
questions.explanation: All others are perfect squares (11², 13², 14², 15²); 250 is not.

questions.topic: Logical reasoning & mental ability
questions.question: In a certain code, COLD is written as DQOH. How is WARM written in that code?
questions.explanation: Letters are shifted forward by +1, +2, +3, +4: W→X, A→C, R→U, M→Q, giving XCUQ.

questions.topic: Logical reasoning & mental ability
questions.question: If MANGO is coded as NBOHP, how is APPLE coded?
questions.explanation: Each letter moves one step forward: A→B, P→Q, P→Q, L→M, E→F.

questions.topic: Logical reasoning & mental ability
questions.question: Pointing to a man, Lakshmi said, “He is the son of my grandfather's only son.” How is the man related to Lakshmi?
questions.explanation: Her grandfather's only son is her father; his son is her brother.

questions.topic: Logical reasoning & mental ability
questions.question: A is the sister of B. C is the mother of B. D is the father of C. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation: A is a daughter of C (as B's sister), and C is D's daughter, so A is D's granddaughter.

questions.topic: Logical reasoning & mental ability
questions.question: Statements: All engineers are graduates. Some graduates are teachers. Conclusions: I. Some engineers are teachers. II. Some teachers are graduates. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: II is the converse of ‘some graduates are teachers’, so it follows. I need not follow: the graduates who are teachers may not include any engineers.

questions.topic: Logical reasoning & mental ability
questions.question: Statements: All cats are dogs. No dog is a rat. Conclusions: I. No cat is a rat. II. Some rats are cats. Which conclusion(s) follow?
questions.explanation: Every cat is inside ‘dogs’, and dogs and rats do not overlap, so no cat is a rat. II therefore cannot follow.

questions.topic: Logical reasoning & mental ability
questions.question: Statement: “Use public transport to reduce traffic congestion” — an appeal by the city traffic police. Assumptions: I. Many people will respond to the appeal. II. Public transport occupies less road space per passenger than private vehicles. Which assumption(s) are implicit?
options: Both I and II are implicit
questions.explanation: An appeal is made expecting a response (I), and recommending public transport for congestion assumes it uses less road space per passenger (II).

questions.topic: Logical reasoning & mental ability
questions.question: If 1 January 2026 was a Thursday, what day of the week is 1 January 2027?
questions.explanation: 2026 is not a leap year, so it has 365 days = 52 weeks + 1 odd day. The day advances by one: Thursday → Friday.

questions.topic: Quantitative aptitude, basic maths & data interpretation
questions.question: A can finish a work in 12 days and B in 18 days. Working together, in how many days will they finish it?
questions.explanation: Combined rate = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 per day, so time = 36/5 = 7.2 days.

questions.topic: Quantitative aptitude, basic maths & data interpretation
questions.question: A and B together can do a job in 10 days; A alone can do it in 15 days. In how many days can B alone do it?
questions.explanation: B's rate = 1/10 − 1/15 = 1/30, so B takes 30 days.

questions.topic: Quantitative aptitude, basic maths & data interpretation
questions.question: A pipe can fill a tank in 20 minutes and another can empty it in 30 minutes. If both are opened together on an empty tank, it will be full in
questions.explanation: Net rate = 1/20 − 1/30 = 1/60 per minute, so 60 minutes.

questions.question: A 240 m long train crosses a 360 m long platform in 30 seconds. Its speed is
questions.explanation: Distance = 240 + 360 = 600 m in 30 s = 20 m/s = 72 km/h. (Forgetting the platform gives 28.8; forgetting to convert gives 20.)

questions.topic: Quantitative aptitude, basic maths & data interpretation
questions.question: A car goes from A to B at 60 km/h and returns at 40 km/h. Its average speed for the whole journey is
questions.explanation: For equal distances, average speed = 2xy/(x + y) = 2×60×40/100 = 48 km/h — not the arithmetic mean 50.

questions.topic: Quantitative aptitude, basic maths & data interpretation
questions.question: The average of five numbers is 24. If one number is removed, the average of the rest becomes 22. The number removed is
questions.explanation: Total = 5 × 24 = 120; remaining total = 4 × 22 = 88; removed = 32.

questions.topic: Quantitative aptitude, basic maths & data interpretation
questions.question: For the data 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9, which of the following is correct (population variance)?
questions.explanation: Mean = 40/8 = 5; mode = 4 (occurs three times); variance = Σ(x − 5)²/8 = 32/8 = 4, so the standard deviation is 2.

questions.topic: Quantitative aptitude, basic maths & data interpretation
questions.question: A district's paddy production (thousand tonnes) was: 2021 — 400, 2022 — 460, 2023 — 437, 2024 — 520. In which year was the percentage increase over the previous year the highest?
questions.explanation: 2022: +60/400 = 15%; 2023: −23/460 = −5%; 2024: +83/437 ≈ 19%. The highest growth is in 2024 — a larger absolute rise on a smaller base.

questions.question: The median and mode of 4, 8, 6, 5, 3, 8, 9 are respectively
questions.explanation: Sorted: 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 8, 9 — the middle (4th) value is 6; 8 occurs most often.
